ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and Regulations SOR/2002-184; FINTRAC supervisory framework; Criminal Code (Canada) money-laundering and terrorist-financing offences; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. Provincial: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (arts. 17–33 and 356–360 governing names, registered office, records and filings); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (arts. 12–14, 21.1–21.4 and 36–37.1 governing registration and confidential beneficial-owner disclosure); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11; Act respecting private employment placement agencies, RLRQ c L-6.1, if applicable. Federal alternative: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 106.3 register of individuals with significant control.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access – the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec receives beneficial-owner information in the enterprise registration declaration pursuant to P-44.1 art. 21.1; the beneficial-owner dataset is confidential, not displayed in the public registry, but is accessible to FINTRAC, the Canada Revenue Agency, law enforcement and authorized regulatory bodies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution) and Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (in force for Canada since 14 January 2024); Quebec-issued documents are apostilled by the Ministere de la Justice du Quebec, federal documents by Global Affairs Canada; for non-Hague destinations, full consular legalization chain applies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Register / attestation of individuals with significant control, demonstrating 25% ownership or control thresholds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary or corporate secretary at the registered office, based on the confidential REQ declaration and internal corporate register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Quebec notary followed by Hague Apostille through the Ministere de la Justice du Quebec; consular legalization where the receiving state is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Name Reservation or NUANS Name Search Report
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: REQ for Quebec reservation; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada / Corporations Canada for the federal NUANS search
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Global Affairs Canada for federal reports; Ministere de la Justice du Quebec for REQ certificates) or consular legalization as required by the counterparty jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Office certificate and commercial substance attestation (street address in Quebec, mail reception, records custody and physical presence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec registered agent or law firm providing the registered-office service, supported by lease or virtual-office agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation then Hague Apostille (Quebec) or consular legalization for non-Hague receiving states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening at onboarding and at least annually thereafter of all beneficial owners, directors, officers, counsel and client-facing counterparties against: (1) FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons and Heads of International Organizations (PEP/HIO) guidelines under PCMLTFA s. 9.6; (2) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list; (3) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (4) Canadian sanctions regulations administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (5) Criminal Code (Canada) money-laundering and financing-of-terrorism provisions. Suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC is mandatory within statutory timelines; enhanced due diligence applies automatically where a PEP, sanctions hit or high-risk jurisdiction is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec online portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal combined name search via the Corporations Canada / ISED NUANS portal if incorporating under the CBCA and later registering extra-provincially in Quebec
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under P-44.1 and S-31.1, a Quebec business corporation name must be in French, or in French together with another language, and must satisfy REQ traceability and distinctiveness requirements. Non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin script using accepted phonetic or conventional forms. A legal element, e.g. Inc., Corp., Ltée or Incorporée, is mandatory. French-language obligations under the Charter of the French Language also govern internal operations where employees are located in Quebec.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Assurance / Insurance (insurance licensing and ministerial prior approval)
Royal / Royale (Crown authorization may be required)
Avocat / Notaire / Barreau (unauthorized practice of law prohibitions)
Courtier / Broker (may trigger securities or insurance brokerage authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ name refusal, the applicant may file a new reservation request with a distinct conventional or completely distinctive variant, or file a revision application with the Registraire within 60 days under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (P-44.1, s. 72), and thereafter appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Quebec. For federal CBCA filings, an administrative reconsideration may be addressed to the Director of Corporations Canada. The 90-day reservation is not renewable; after expiry, a fresh REQ/ISED search and reservation application must be completed before statutory filing of the articles.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for a low-risk executive-search retainer boutique: the Quebec Business Corporations Act (S-31.1, art. 356) requires a registered-office municipality with a genuine street address in Quebec capable of receiving legal process and statutory records, and a professional virtual-office service satisfying that standard is legally permissible. However, exclusive reliance on a virtual office without any physical or administrative substance may provoke a CRA Quebec income-tax residence review and heightened REQ or banking KYC scrutiny; a physical office in Montreal, Quebec City or another commercial center is recommended where the headhunting activity involves payroll, proprietary client data or government contracts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — quantified annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by REQ, CRA or Quebec workplace regulators is estimated at 8% for a standard non-financial services entity; probability rises to approximately 30% where a beneficial owner or director appears on a PEP or watch-list, where REQ initiates a targeted administrative audit, or where the client base includes high-risk foreign jurisdictions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, including provisions governing constitution, articles, registered office, directors, officers, shares, and corporate records; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, including enterprise registration and updating obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), administered by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for constitution of a Québec business corporation, together with articles of incorporation and the initial enterprise registration filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Québec business corporation, and no statutory escrow account is required. Shares may be issued for cash, property, or services of legally acceptable value. The corporation must maintain evidence of subscriptions, consideration received, and issued share ownership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation accept and record the subscription by the incorporator for the issued common shares specified in the subscription agreement, against receipt of the agreed consideration. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Corporation be established at the Quebec address stated in the articles and maintained in the corporate records. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed President and Secretary, and that [Name] be appointed Treasurer, each to serve until resignation, replacement, or removal in accordance with law. RESOLVED that the officers are authorized to complete registry, banking, tax, employment, and licensing registrations and to execute all related documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select and Clear the Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Choose a compliant French corporate name or a numbered corporation. For a word name, conduct the required name search and confirm distinctiveness, linguistic compliance, and absence of misleading or prohibited terms. Reserve or submit the name with the incorporation application. Obtain consent or supporting evidence where the selected name includes a controlled term or a third-party element.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-corporation designation
Name search report or supporting name analysis
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name, supporting distinctiveness evidence, or a numbered-corporation alternative. Refile the application and pay any applicable amendment or resubmission charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online incorporation service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles, registered office details, share structure, restrictions on share transfers if required, and director information. Identify the incorporator and provide required declarations. Submit the incorporation application electronically, pay the regular or priority fee, and retain the electronic acknowledgement and filing receipt. Notarization is generally not required for standard electronic Quebec incorporation documents; notarize or legalize foreign corporate powers of attorney and certified identity documents where requested.
required_dossiers: Share structure and share subscription terms
Foreign authorization, notarization, or legalization documents where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry query within the stated deadline, correct defective articles or identification data, and resubmit through the REQ portal. Obtain a written refusal reason and seek administrative reconsideration or judicial review only after completing the available filing cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Enterprise Registration and Beneficial Ownership Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and its enterprise registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the Québec enterprise number, file the required initial declaration of registration, disclose directors, officers, controlling individuals, and other prescribed information, and identify establishments and assumed names. File updates promptly following changes in directors, address, control, or activities. Maintain the corporate register, securities register, minute book, resolutions, and share subscription records at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete or inconsistent enterprise information through an amendment filing. If a filing is rejected or a compliance notice is issued, provide supporting corporate records and request registry correction or review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Organizational Resolutions and Issue Shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's registered office; no separate government approval is required for routine organizational resolutions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or execute written resolutions of the incorporator, directors, and shareholders where applicable. Adopt the registered office, appoint officers, approve the banking mandate, approve the business plan and fiscal year, authorize tax registrations, and issue shares against documented consideration. Record certificates or uncertificated securities, update the securities register, and preserve proof of payment.
required_dossiers: Share certificates or uncertificated security statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pass corrective board or shareholder resolutions, rectify the securities register, and document any late or defective issuance. Obtain legal advice before issuing shares for non-cash consideration or services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Personnel Placement Agency Licence and Operating Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST), through the personnel placement agency licensing process.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before supplying candidates or charging placement fees, determine whether the business falls within the regulated personnel placement agency definition. Submit the licence application, prescribed fee, corporate information, Quebec address, responsible-person information, and required attestations. Establish written client and candidate processes, fee disclosures, record retention, privacy controls, and anti-reprisal procedures. If recruiting temporary foreign workers, obtain any additional applicable authorization and comply with Quebec and federal immigration rules.
required_dossiers: CNESST personnel placement agency licence application
REQ enterprise registration and corporate certificate
Articles and corporate resolution authorizing the application
Temporary foreign worker authorization documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Do not conduct regulated placement activity while an application is incomplete or refused. Cure deficiencies by submitting missing evidence, corrected declarations, or an updated responsible-person file. Request CNESST review or appeal a formal refusal under the applicable administrative process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Premises, Employment, and Municipal Operating Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of the registered or operating premises, CNESST, Revenu Québec, Canada Revenue Agency, and applicable building or fire authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify zoning and permitted office use before occupancy. Obtain municipal occupancy, signage, or business permits where required. Register as an employer with CNESST when employing workers, establish payroll and source-deduction accounts, and implement occupational health and safety procedures. Confirm commercial lease, insurance, data-security, and client-record safeguards.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct zoning, occupancy, safety, or employer-registration deficiencies before commencing the affected activity. Request municipal inspection, CNESST correction guidance, or an administrative review of a formal adverse decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST), for the Quebec personnel placement agency licence; municipal authorities regulate premises and occupancy.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'agence de placement de personnel (Personnel Placement Agency Licence). The licence is generally relevant where the business places or assigns workers with client employers for remuneration; a pure executive-search advisory service may require a scope determination based on its actual activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary office-based executive-search operations; no industrial project, manufacturing process, or environmental impact assessment is ordinarily triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific industrial wastewater, VOC, or process-emission thresholds ordinarily apply to an office-based agency. The business must comply with municipal sewer and waste rules, the Environment Quality Act where applicable, hazardous-material storage and disposal requirements, and general prohibitions against unauthorized releases. Any future laboratory, warehouse, vehicle fleet, or industrial activity requires separate environmental screening.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal occupancy or change-of-use approval where required, comply with applicable Quebec building and fire-safety requirements, maintain unobstructed exits and emergency procedures, and complete fire inspection or certification if required by the municipality or building authority. Structural load inspection is generally unnecessary for ordinary office use but is required if premises modifications, heavy storage, server installations, or altered occupancy create a structural concern. Register with CNESST when employing workers and implement workplace health and safety, ergonomic, emergency, and incident-reporting procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/businesses.html) and Revenu Québec via the CLICK business portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca); legal entity registration is effected through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca), which issues the NEQ (Québec Enterprise Number) used as the master business identifier for all tax accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate federally or provincially and complete legal publicity before the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ and certificate of registration. 2) Apply to the CRA for a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) with program accounts (RC corporate income tax, RT GST/HST, RP payroll) using Form RC1 or Business Registration Online; a Canadian-incorporated corporation is resident for tax purposes and obtains the BN before filing its T2 return. 3) File Form LM-1-V or register online in CLICK with Revenu Québec to open the Quebec tax dossier, which integrates the QST account, Quebec corporate income tax account (CO-17), and source deduction accounts under the same BN. 4) For a foreign entity carrying on business in Quebec, first complete extra-provincial registration and obtain an attestation of registration; a foreign corporation may then obtain a BN and register for QST/GST without maintaining a physical establishment in Canada, but must appoint an agent for service. 5) Revenu Québec administers the federal GST/HST for Quebec-based businesses under the federal-provincial harmonization agreement, so the first-time registrant completes a single registration file covering both GST and QST. 6) Re-open or amend program accounts through CRA Business Registration Online and Revenu Québec CLICK whenever ownership, directors, address, or payroll status changes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian resident corporation taxed on worldwide income under ITA s. 2 with integrated federal and Quebec corporate income tax; executive search and headhunting fees are taxable business income; no territorial remittance exemption for the head office; the corporation may qualify as a Canadian-controlled private corporation, entitling it to the small business deduction on active business income up to the business limit).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime; classification is statutory. Available elections include: non-calendar fiscal period election under ITA s. 249.1(1)(b); GST/HST closely related corporation election under ETA s. 156 eliminating tax on intercorporate supplies; mirror QST closely related person election under the QSTA; GST/HST quick method election under ETA s. 227 for small suppliers; QST quick method (méthode rapide) election for small businesses; ITA s. 85 rollover elections for transfers of property to the corporation; FAPI designation and s. 93(1) dividend election for hybrid-mismatch alignment with controlled foreign affiliates; and ITA s. 216 election for rental or timber income of non-residents where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT-type dual consumption tax: federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax under the Excise Tax Act (5% GST in Quebec; Quebec is not an HST province) plus Quebec Sales Tax under the An Act respecting the Québec sales tax (QST, administered by Revenu Québec); Quebec-based registrants file a combined GST/HST and QST return with Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual worldwide taxable supplies threshold over any four consecutive calendar quarters; this small-supplier threshold applies to both GST/HST and QST and includes taxable supplies of associated persons; once exceeded, the executive search corporation must register for GST/HST and QST and collect 14.975% combined tax on taxable Canadian services, with a corresponding obligation for non-resident persons carrying on taxable activity in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices exists in Canada. Quebec is phasing in mandatory Peppol-based e-invoicing and e-reporting: from September 1, 2025, enterprises with annual revenue above CAD 100 million must accept e-invoices, and from September 1, 2026, they must issue e-invoices through certified service providers using Peppol BIS 3.0; mandatory phases for mid-market enterprises (CAD 10 million to 100 million) and smaller businesses are scheduled to follow from 2027 to 2028. A specialized executive search agency below these thresholds may continue to issue paper or PDF invoices, but must retain transactional data to support future e-reporting and must comply with Revenu Québec record-keeping standards; GST/HST and QST registration numbers must appear on all invoices issued in Canada.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of executive search and headhunting services to a non-resident client is zero-rated for GST/HST purposes under Part V of Schedule VI, section 7(a)(i) of the Excise Tax Act when the client is not registered for GST/HST, the service is not supplied to the client while physically present in Canada, and the service is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada; the corresponding QST zero-rating rule applies to the same non-resident supply under the mirror provisions of the QSTA. Zero-rating is also available where the non-resident recipient is registered if the service is acquired exclusively for use in a commercial activity carried on outside Canada. Domestic search placements, candidate introductions, and retainer services performed for Canadian employers or Canadian subsidiaries of foreign clients attract full GST plus QST at 14.975%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A or ACI eManifest) - generally not applicable to cross-border services, but required if any ancillary physical deliverables are exported
Bill of Lading or airway bill - only for physical documentary or marketing materials accompanying the service
Inward remittance certificate and SWIFT/MT103 or Wise B2B payment trace proving receipt of the foreign retainer without domestic on-invoicing
Signed executive search contract or statement of work identifying the non-resident client, its foreign jurisdiction, and the fee currency
Invoice marked zero-rated export supply under ETA Schedule VI Part V section 7 and the QSTA non-resident service provision
Evidence of where the recruitment services were performed, including candidate location assessments and remote delivery records
Full retention of the above documentation for a minimum of six years under ITA s. 230 and ETA s. 286
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reverse zero-rating on audit where services are in fact consumed in Canada, such as where the foreign client is a conduit for a Canadian operation or where the headhunting activity places candidates with a Canadian affiliate; reassessments are retrospective to the date of the original claim and attract full GST and QST, compounded daily interest, and penalties. Canada does not impose a statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, but documentary evidence must exist at the time of the claim and be retained for six years; failure to repatriate or substantiate may be treated as an inaccurate claim. Gross negligence carries a 50% penalty on the tax amount under ETA s. 285(1) and the QSTA equivalent, wilful evasion carries a 100% civil penalty, the limitation period is unlimited in cases of misrepresentation, and criminal prosecution is possible under ETA s. 239 and the QSTA; recovery may be enforced against corporate assets through Revenu Québec legal hypothec and collection powers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC); with OSFI as banking prudential regulator and FINTRAC as the AML/CFT and cross-border wire report authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under a freely floating exchange-rate regime; there are no exchange controls restricting conversion, remittance, or foreign-currency pricing. Profit remittance via dividends is unrestricted but subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax at a statutory 25% rate, generally reduced by tax treaty (e.g., 5–15% under the Canada-US or Canada-France treaties) and dependent on timely T106/T1134 informational filings where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Canada. Cross-border service revenues may be retained in any currency; however, financial institutions automatically report every transaction over CAD 10,000 to FINTRAC, and Canadian-controlled corporations with foreign-currency accounts or foreign property costing over CAD 100,000 must file the T1135 form with their corporate income tax return.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for B2B settlement via Wise Business (Wise Payments Ltd., registered as a Money Services Business with FINTRAC). Legal constraints: Wise is not a Schedule I/II bank, holds no CDIC deposit coverage, and multi-currency balances are pooled/non-segregated; thus Wise is suitable only as a secondary collections/disbursement rail, not as a capital-escrow or regulatory-capital depository.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec-registered Canadian business corporation with resident directors, remote onboarding is generally permitted at Tier-1 banks using digital KYC. However, when opening a capital-escrow account or when any ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident, the bank will typically require at least one authorized signatory to attend an in-person identity interview at a Canadian branch, supplemented by notarized corporate resolutions and certified UBO documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO or foreign parent entity controlling more than 25% of the Quebec corporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, certificates of corporate existence for each entity in the ownership chain, register of directors and shareholders with UBO declaration, source-of-wealth narrative, tax residency certificates of the UBOs, and an organizational chart validated by a CPA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client payments originating from high-risk sectors, sanctioned jurisdictions, or politically exposed persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed executive-search retainer agreements, invoicing with precise service descriptions, the Quebec employment-agency statutory licence, and a documented sanctions-screening policy aligned with FINTRAC transaction-monitoring obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid pass-through flows: large inbound retainer wires followed by immediate disbursements to third-party candidates or overseas contractors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month cash-flow forecast, underlying search and placement agreements, candidate employment contracts, and a treasury policy capping daily flows with source-of-funds verification for each inbound payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on fintech rails such as Wise B2B for volumes exceeding the bank's internal concentration thresholds or for escrow purposes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of Wise's FINTRAC MSB registration, platform audit trail, fund-segregation confirmation, and a documented fallback clearing plan with a Schedule I bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-debt wires must route via SWIFT MT103 using BPM6 purpose codes: Equity injection/paid-in capital (code 5220) or shareholder loan (code 5330). The remitter must be the named shareholder and the beneficiary field must show the corporation's 9-digit CRA Business Number. Foreign direct investment resulting in control triggers Investment Canada Act notification where applicable, and Statistics Canada direct-investment surveys must be completed if served; all transfers over CAD 10,000 are captured by FINTRAC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Retainer and placement-fee disbursements to non-resident contractors and candidates clear via SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 payment) referencing 'Management consulting services – executive search fee'. Wise B2B may be used for lower-value disbursements through local clearing rails (EFT, ACH, and Faster Payments equivalents based on destination currency). Commercial letters of credit are not appropriate for executive-search services and should not be used; bank-guaranteed wire transfers are the acceptable clearing rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts (up to 24-month tenor) with a Schedule I bank under ISDA/CSA credit documentation
Vanilla FX options (puts and calls on CAD or USD), including collars and zero-premium structures, for balance-sheet hedging
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) to convert foreign-currency-denominated debt or contract receivables into CAD cash flows, subject to board approval
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible or necessary in Canada because CAD is fully convertible; any hedging must settle on a deliverable basis

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 35; additional recurring penalties; after 12 months of default the corporation may be administratively struck off and then dissolved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employment Agency Licence Renewal (executive-search and headhunting placement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of licence issuance; renewal must be filed before the licence expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Expiration of licence immediately prohibits paid placement activities in Quebec; continuing operations after expiry triggers cease-and-desist orders and administrative fines up to CAD 15,000 for an individual and CAD 50,000 for a corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporate Annual Return (applicable only to a corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act; for a provincial Quebec corporation this item is not required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late fee is prescribed, but failure to file for one year may cause the Director to dissolve the corporation without further formalities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Register Confirmation (share transfer and beneficial ownership update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual declaration; any share transfer must be registered in the register of members within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate beneficial ownership information can lead to administrative penalties up to CAD 15,000 and personal liability for officers and directors under Quebec's register transparency regime.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Quebec private business corporation is exempt from a mandatory independent auditor appointment if it is not a reporting issuer and does not have publicly traded securities. Despite the general exemption, an auditor must be appointed if shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting shares make a written requisition, or if the corporation is governed by the Canada Business Corporations Act and an exemption by special resolution has not been obtained.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for defined reporting issuers; private corporations may prepare financial statements in accordance with Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, quarterly financial statements need not be filed publicly but must be prepared for shareholder meetings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec corporate law requires the annual declaration to include a current list of directors and, through the confidential corporate registry process, confirmation that the register of members and beneficial ownership information are up to date. Any share transfer during the year must be recorded in the register of members within 30 days. The registraire can disclose beneficial ownership information to tax authorities and regulators; public access exists under Quebec's beneficial ownership transparency rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Corporate Minute Book containing articles, by-laws, resolutions and share transfer records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: If an audit is triggered: 3,000–9,000. In most exempt private Quebec corporations only a review engagement (1,500–4,500) is needed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined Canadian federal (15% net general rate after abatement and general rate reduction) and Quebec (11.5% general corporate rate); a qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) claiming the federal and Quebec small business deductions is taxed at an effective combined rate of 14% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction (19 percentage point reduction on active business income up to CAD 500,000); Quebec small business deduction (reduction of Quebec corporate rate from 11.5% to 5% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income); provincial abatement (10% of Part I federal tax allocable to Canadian provinces); general rate reduction (13% for non-CCPCs); refundable SR&ED investment tax credits for qualifying CCPCs; GST/HST and QST input tax credits on business expenses. SBD and the Quebec reduced rate are unavailable to corporations controlled by non-residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Corporation Internet Filing (CIF) system through certified EFILE software; Quebec: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return transmitted electronically to Revenu Québec through its accredited e-filing service; annual declaration of legal publicity filed with the Quebec Registraire des entreprises (using the NEQ-issued number).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a corporation must file for every fiscal year, including short first-year periods; the fiscal period cannot exceed 53 weeks (12 months + interim period).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 and CO-17 returns are due no later than six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end is due by June 30 of the following calendar year); the final balance of federal and Quebec income tax payable is due two months after fiscal year-end, extended to three months for a qualifying CCPC with an active business limit; instalment payments are generally due on the 15th day of each month where prior-year federal/Quebec tax exceeds CAD 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, CRA business number (BN), Canada Revenue Agency account, registered office address, and fiscal period end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must obtain a BN by filing Form RC431 and quote the BN on all returns; provide the Canadian agent's name and address for service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income from executive search retainers, success fees, and placement commissions; net income for income tax purposes after reconciliation of accounting income to tax basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment (PE); apply treaty PE thresholds and allocate revenues and expenses consistent with Articles 7/9 of the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions under sections 110 to 113 (loss carryforwards, intercorporate dividends, foreign exchange adjustments, etc.).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers compute taxable income from Canadian-source business income under Part I; capital gains/losses are reportable on Schedule 7 with treaty override where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Part I tax on taxable income: base 38%, provincial abatement 10%, general rate reduction 13%, and additional credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents cannot claim the M&P (manufacturing and processing) deduction unless qualified; claim the foreign tax credit on Schedule 21 for foreign-source taxes attributable to income taxed in both Canada and the residence state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal SBD claim on active business income up to CAD 500,000, prorated for short fiscal periods, subject to taxable capital phase-out (CAD 10 million to CAD 15 million) and associated corporation aggregation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation controlled, directly or indirectly, by one or more non-resident persons is not a CCPC and cannot claim the SBD; the full 26.5% combined rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 – Part A, Line 30/Line 60 (Quebec income and tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income and tax calculation using the general rate of 11.5% or the reduced rate of 5% for qualifying CCPCs; Quebec Schedule B (annex B) for the small business deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned corporation with a Quebec PE must file CO-17 and allocate Quebec taxable income using the Quebec allocation formula; claim Quebec foreign tax credits, if applicable, in CO-16.1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T106 Information Return (Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies reportable cross-border transactions with non-arm's length non-residents, e.g., management fees, commission-sharing, sub-contracting and royalty payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required when the total fair market value of reportable transactions with a non-resident exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year; attach transfer pricing documentation and contemporaneous comparables; file by the statutory return due date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay, capped at 12 months (federal and Quebec); if an amount is assessed after 18 months, the penalty escalates to 10% plus 2% per month for up to 20 months under section 162 of the Income Tax Act and equivalent Quebec provisions. Interest is compounded daily at prescribed CRA and Revenu Québec rates. Gross negligence penalties under s. 163(2) (federal) of 50% of the understated tax, and Quebec counterparts, apply. Criminal prosecution for evasion under s. 239 can result in fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. Late payment of instalments invokes separate arrears interest and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to non-residents, reduced by tax treaty to typically 5% for a corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the voting power of the Canadian corporation and 15% for portfolio dividends; Quebec does not impose a separate dividend withholding tax, as Part XIII is administered federally.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident corporate shareholder must (i) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of its residence jurisdiction; (ii) complete and provide to the Canadian payer CRA Form NR302 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty for a Non-Resident Corporation) together with an organizational chart evidencing 10% voting control and any limitation-on-benefits (LOB) supporting documents; (iii) submit the TRC and NR302 before the dividend payment so the payer may apply the reduced treaty rate at source; (iv) the payer must remit the withheld Part XIII tax to CRA by the 15th day of the following month and issue an NR4 information return; (v) if the full 25% was withheld in error, the non-resident may file Form NR7-R (Refund of Part XIII Tax) within three years of the original payment. Quebec adopts the same treaty rates by virtue of Canada's tax treaty network and its coordination agreements with the CRA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding on cross-border royalties is 25%; most Canadian DTAs reduce royalty withholding to 10% (e.g., Canada-US treaty Article XII, Canada-France, Canada-Germany). Statutory withholding on interest is also 25%, but the Canada-US treaty reduces arm's length interest to 0% and non-arm's length interest to 15%; numerous other treaties reduce interest to 10%. For an executive search/headhunting corporation, royalty payments may arise from licensed recruitment databases, candidate-search software, or employment-assessment tools; ensure the payee provides treaty documentation and that the Canadian payer reports all such cross-border payments on Form NR4.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 (aggregate fair market value of reportable non-arm's length cross-border transactions with a particular non-resident triggering mandatory Form T106 filing); for Country-by-Country Reporting the threshold is CAD 750,000,000 of consolidated group revenue; CRA may require contemporaneous Local File and Master File-style documentation and comparability analysis under Information Circular IC 87-2R for any controlled transaction, irrespective of transaction size, upon audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not impose offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) on domestic operating corporations; however, the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act denies tax benefits of transactions lacking economic substance, and the sham and substance-over-form doctrines permit CRA and courts to disregard artificial contractual arrangements. An executive search agency must demonstrate genuine operational substance: physical office, full-time recruiters on payroll, active solicitation contracts, Canadian client-facing invoicing, corporate records, and board decisions made in Canada. Corporate residence is determined by central management and control; a Quebec-incorporated entity managed from abroad is still tax-resident in Canada for domestic purposes, but treaty interpretation may allocate the profits to a foreign PE. For non-resident shareholders, treaty benefits require real commercial substance in the residence state and compliance with anti-conduit and LOB provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or falsification of retainer and success-fee revenue, off-book cash commissions, use of foreign shell accounts, false invoicing, or filing returns with materially incomplete disclosure of Canadian-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment for all years not statute-barred; gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under s. 163(2) ITA and Quebec Taxation Act equivalents; criminal prosecution under s. 239 ITA, carrying fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to two years (summary) or five years (indictable); CRA may also impose penalties for failure to file T106 and failure to withhold Part XIII.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unremitted source deductions, GST/HST, QST, and Part XIII withholdings under ITA s. 227.1, Excise Tax Act s. 323, and Quebec Tax Administration Act; where evasion involves deliberate concealment, Quebec's Civil Code allows piercing of the corporate veil (art. 317 CCQ) for fraud and abuse of rights, exposing directors' personal assets to civil restitution and freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of the headhunting business as a shell with no staff, no Canadian office, nominee directors, minimal board records, and channelling of placement fees through an intermediary in a low-tax or no-tax jurisdiction without business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under s. 245 re-characterizes or disallows the tax benefit; assessment of the full 26.5% federal/Quebec rate on the disallowed income; 50% gross negligence penalty; potential cancellation of corporate registration under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act for failure to file annual returns; consequential loss of treaty entitlements and possible criminal exposure for fraudulent misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling shareholders are personally liable for the unpaid taxes where the corporation is a 'persona ficta' facade; CRA can collect against the shareholder who receives the diverted income; courts may issue asset freezes and civil restitution orders; directors of federally registered companies may be disqualified or barred from serving as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payment of excessive management, consulting, or database-access fees to a non-arm's length non-resident affiliate (e.g., 20% of headhunting gross revenue to an offshore related party with no functional or factual substance) without contemporaneous benchmarking; failure to file Form T106 for reportable cross-border transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under s. 247(2) ITA; penalty under s. 247(3) of 10% of the net adjustment, minimum CAD 5,000 (maximum penalty does not apply where reasonable efforts and contemporaneous documentation exist); late T106 filing penalties of CAD 300 for each month of non-filing up to 25 months? (In practice, prescribed penalties under s. 162(10.1) apply); denial of expense deduction, reallocation of income, and potential reassessment of withholding tax on deemed dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or negligently approved the non-arm's length arrangements may be held personally liable for penalties and interest under the Quebec Tax Administration Act and for gross negligence under the Income Tax Act; where the inflated fees were routed personally to the director, the CRA may pierce the veil and attach the director's assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold Part XIII tax on dividends, royalties, or interest paid/credited to non-residents; failure to remit Quebec payroll source deductions (income tax, QPIP, CNESST, CSST), federal source deductions, and GST/HST/QST collected on taxable supplies of headhunting services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA and Revenu Québec collect the gross amounts unremitted plus prescribed statutory interest compounded daily; penalty for non-remittance of 10% of the deficiency when more than once in a 24-month period; criminal charges for non-remittance of source deductions under s. 227(4.1) ITA carry fines of up to CAD 50,000 and/or two years' imprisonment for a first offence; Quebec administrative fines are imposed under the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the entire amount of unremitted source deductions under s. 227.1 ITA and s. 323 ETA, without the protection of limited liability; the 'due diligence' defence is narrowly construed; CRA may issue a director's assessment, register a lien, seize personal property, and enforce garnishments; travel restrictions and exit bans are possible where a director has been charged with a criminal tax offence.
